title: Building a comprehensively annotated and sequenced immune oncology NSCLC cohort
summary: The aim of this study is to understand why lung cancer patients respond differently to immunotherapies. Immunotherapies are treatments that activate the body's own immune system to fight the tumor. With immunotherapies, some patients can be treated successfully for a very long time. However, not all patients respond equally well to these treatments, and the reasons for this are still unclear. We assume that the type and number of mutations, the varying activities of signaling pathways, and the composition of different cell types within the tumor are responsible for the therapy response. We therefore intend to compare these factors in patients who respond very well to immunotherapy with those in patients who respond less well. In this way, we may be able to select alternative therapies in the future for patients who are likely to respond less favorably. In addition, the findings of our study may contribute to the development of new therapies.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung

interventions.name: Genomic and transcriptomic analyses are being conducted on patients with advanced non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who are receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy, in order to identify characteristics associated with the response to ICI.
